# `phasegradient`

a band's phase gradient from its cross-spectrum through a free kernel, as the additive ingredients of the surface's leaves.

Version 2, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run phasegradient --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run phasegradient --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run phasegradient --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --cross-spectrum rest_crossspectrum --band alpha --kernel KERNEL --finest "parts 16"
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `cross_spectrum` | statistic welch, where {"name": "$cross_spectrum"} | yes |
| `kernel` | operator inverse kernel, where {"name": "$kernel"} | yes |
| `surface` | manifold surface, is kernel.to | yes |
| `frames` | field canonical frames, manifold kernel.to (the canonical frames of the kernel's surface (`nxr-neuro run surface_frames` first)) | yes |
| `leaves` | selection ladder, manifold kernel.to (the surface's grid (`nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface` first)) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cross_spectrum` | `--cross-spectrum` | none | - |  | the band cross-spectrum's name (a statistic made by crossspectrum) |
| `band` | `--band` | none | - |  | the band of the cross-spectrum (its name); null: its one band |
| `kernel` | `--kernel` | `none` | - |  | the free-orientation inverse kernel's name, or none: the subject's one inverse kernel |
| `finest` | `--finest` | `parts 16` | mm |  | the leaves measured, as a quantity: a tile diameter (mm), a tile area (mm2) or parts per hemisphere (the level is resolved in closed form and recorded with the snapped quantity) |
| `signal` | `--signal` | none | - | normal, ambient | NO DEFAULT (an orientation prior is never a default): the caller states it. normal = the current along the surface's normal \| ambient = each of its x y z components |
| `name` | `--name` | `{cross_spectrum}_{kernel}_phasegradient_{band}` | - |  | the name of the field the measurements are of |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`meeg.phase_gradient`](../nodes.md) | cross_spectrum=cross_spectrum, kernel=kernel, surface=surface, frames=frames, leaves=leaves | band=$band, signal=$signal, finest=$finest | phase, ingredients |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `phase` | kind field, kind_name phase gradient, name $name, on kernel.to |
| `ingredients` | kind measurement, over leaves, of phase |

## Notes from the definition

```text
A BAND'S PHASE GRADIENT AS THE PYRAMID'S LEAF INGREDIENTS (measurements of a field with no array, over a level of the surface's ladder): from a stored band cross-spectrum
(`nxr-neuro run crossspectrum --channels-of KERNEL` first) and the free kernel, the signal's rows (the normal current, or each ambient component) and their tangent P1 gradients
give per vertex the power P, the phase current H and the gradient power Q; H is read in the canonical frames (`nxr-neuro run surface_frames` first); per leaf of the grid level stated as `finest` (a quantity: the surface's grid,
`nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface` first), by `reduce` over that level, the sums weighted by the vertex's lumped area. The gradient, the travelling index and the speed are ratios derived at read.
The kernel spreads each source over its neighbours with no lag: that shrinks the phase gradient, so the speed is overestimated where the spread is wide.

  nxr-neuro run phasegradient --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --cross-spectrum rest_crossspectrum --band alpha --kernel KERNEL --finest "parts 16"
```
